items.snippet: October 10, 1993: Apple ships its Macintosh Color Classic II, the last of the 9-inch compact Macs. Its predecessor, the original Macintosh Color Classic, debuted in February 1993. The first Mac to come with a built-in color monitor, the gorgeous machine allowed for Apple IIe emulation courtesy of a PDS card. “In many ways, the Color Classic is the compact Mac everyone’s been waiting for since, well, since 1984,” MacUser magazine wrote in April 1993. However, in unintended “classic” fashion, it harked back to the original 1984 Macintosh in one other way. It was a beautiful computer, but horribly underpowered. Instead of treating the Color Classic as a gorgeous retro throwback experiment (which, let’s face it, isn’t any more niche than a lot of the other ideas Apple was trying at this time), Apple instead forced the computer to occupy a spot as an entry-level machine. items.title: Diamond Rapids will be Intel’s last Xeon with SGX as TDX takes over
items.snippet: Intel will end new Xeon support for Software Guard Extensions (SGX) after Diamond Rapids, making Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) the focus of its confidential-computing roadmap. items.title: OpenAI grader model tried to wreck its environment to force a reset
items.snippet: An OpenAI model grading seven responses during reinforcement-learning training tried to damage its task environment after discovering the required input files were missing. None of the grades from that attempt was accepted. Source
